supporting_observations.claim: Near the alert time, WS-KNGUYEN-01 made Kerberos connections to the domain controller: one at 13:41:29 UTC and another at 13:42:41 UTC. These connection records do not identify an account-management operation or the user who initiated it.
WS-KNGUYEN-01 also made LDAP connections to the domain controller at 13:31 UTC, but the connection metadata does not reveal what LDAP operation was performed.

known_telemetry_limitations: Winsec and Sysmon collection for WS-KNGUYEN-01 and DC-COP-01 was unavailable from 13:25 through 14:15 UTC. This covers the reported account-creation time, so relevant endpoint and domain-controller events may be missing.
The available Zeek connection records show connection metadata, not the contents or purpose of the Kerberos or LDAP activity (for example, records T117-00062, T117-00080, and T117-00027).
claims_not_established: The supplied records do not establish whether backupadmin was created, or provide a domain-controller account-creation event for it.
The identity of the account creator, the initiating host or session, and whether the activity was authorized are not established.
The account's group memberships, privileges, enabled state, and intended purpose are not established.
additional_evidence_needed: Retrieve the missing DC-COP-01 Winsec events for 13:25–14:15 UTC, especially account-management events, and verify whether backupadmin was created.
Obtain account attributes, group-membership changes, and audit records for backupadmin, including the creator's identity and logon/session details.
Check help-desk and IT change records for an approved account request matching the reported creation time.
unrelated_findings: A Sysmon event records csrss.exe accessing lsass.exe on WS-KNGUYEN-01 at 13:23:31 UTC with GrantedAccess=0x1000. This is outside the reported account-creation time and does not establish a connection to the alert; review separately if warranted. (T117-00017)
